correctness.rationale: The binary-digit parity recurrence proves the 4-letter coding. A 3-state weighted automaton counts exact greedy arches, which equal the fixed-binary-alphabet subsequence universality index by the earliest-embedding argument. All 12 transfer entries are proved by an explicit level-4 base and a one-level morphism induction (including incoming states and final-state behavior). A dyadic interval decomposition, at most two chunks per scale, gives the uniform logarithmic error for every position and length. The exact dyadic values follow from the a-block. Standalone verify.py independently confirms digit coding to length 32768, all transfer entries for 23 levels, direct target-subsequence enumeration on 266 short factors, and the bound on 22890 intervals. Computation is only a finite check; all unbounded quantifiers rest on the induction.

value.rationale: The all-factor uniform statement is a new structural quantitative feature of a classical 2-automatic word and a standard deletion-robustness invariant, not a finite spot check. The exact 5/16 coefficient is calculated by a nontrivial weighted substitution transfer and is valid uniformly over all possible factor locations. The explicit parity correction at dyadic lengths strengthens the asymptotic assertion, and the all-factor bound provides usable quantitative guarantees for arbitrarily far-away factors. The question is motivated by the existing scattered-subsequence universality literature rather than by an ad hoc parameter slice.
